key_insight: Drilled-to-bossed geometry improved AA2024-T351 friction-weld strength, while an ensemble residual network predicted ultimate tensile strength with R² ≈ 0.81.
engineering_relevance: Combining joint geometry design with data-driven prediction could support stronger aluminium joints for aerospace and automotive applications.
method: Tested direct drive friction welding on a customized engine lathe using an L18 orthogonal array.
Varied friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying geometry, and friction time.
Evaluated tensile and torsional strength and compared three deep learning models for tensile-strength prediction.
evidence_signal: The reported optimum—30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, and 4 min friction time—achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify model validation splits or independent testing, so predictive generalization beyond the experimental conditions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
